<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video, scored like a tracker module in which almost every cell is empty. On purpose.</b><br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens. A bottle she throws washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A stray cat drifts in on a crate and falls asleep up the palm. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p, and always daytime.

Read it as a module and it makes perfect sense. Eight channels: her, the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore and the garden (the six lanes in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml)), plus the theme and the ocean. One row per beat at 80 BPM. Every activity waits for the next bar, so every gag lands on the beat, and nearly every cell is a dot, because in a tracker a dot means nothing happens. Nothing happening is the song. In the minute up there, channel 01 gets up, walks off over the water, stays away for 27 rows and comes back with an iced coffee. The song does not notice. More than 90 activities, most of them on four timers, decide when the dots stop, and every sound is synthesized from code, so the sample memory reads 0k. That is accurate.

```
python tools/serve.py
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` for the live preview and the export to a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes the frames, and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.

<pre>
 Key .... Does .......................... Type this
 F1 ..... <a href="MUSING.md">Help, and what was decided</a> .... MUSING.md
 F5 ..... <a href="tools/serve.py">Play, preview, export</a> ......... python tools/serve.py
 F6 ..... <a href="tools/schedule.py">Check and simulate ten hours</a> .. python tools/schedule.py
 F7 ..... <a href="tools/make_audio.py">Synthesize every sound</a> ........ python tools/make_audio.py
 F9 ..... <a href="activities.toml">Load the schedule</a> ............. activities.toml
 F10 .... <a href="tools/render_demo.py">Dev reel, one of everything</a> ... python tools/render_demo.py --dev
 ESC .... Leave ......................... any time. Back with an iced coffee
</pre>

<details>
<summary><b>Order List (F11)</b>: four timers, more than 90 activities, and a great many dots</summary>
<br>

[`activities.toml`](activities.toml) lists more than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-02, and sessions add more every few hours). Most sit on four timers; the rest are chained follow-ups that only start when something else finishes, like the tide that comes for each sandcastle.

| Timer | Goes off every | In a typical 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| super rare | 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 per run | about 2 |

Typical means the median of 200 simulated runs, plus chained follow-ups. She is busy about a third of the time and idling the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so the sea can be busy while she is: the ship has a habit of choosing exactly that moment. Every start snaps to the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds). The default run is `10:00:00` with seed `1992`, and the same seed gives the same video, event for event. `python tools/schedule.py` validates the file and simulates a run.

</details>

<pre>

 02  fishing_quiet      regular     Nibbles. Nothing. The usual.

 05  message_in_bottle  occasional  Thrown. Washes straight back to her feet.

 07  turtle_visit       occasional  A sea turtle crawls up. Both doze off.
 08  coconut_crab       occasional  Lands on a hermit crab. Then it walks off.
 09  cat_visit          rare        Arrives on a crate. Naps up the palm.
 10  delivery_drone     rare        The parcel is another pair of headphones.
 11  signal_hunt        rare        One bar of signal, at the top of the palm.
 12  shark_nod          rare        In headphones, nodding to the same beat.
 13  tour_boat_selfies  rare        Selfies, her in the background. No lift.
 14  efoil_bro          rare        A shaka from a hydrofoil. He carves off.
 15  fire_by_friction   rare        One curl of smoke, one flame, one wave.
 16  hammock            rare        One palm. No second tree. The raft will do.
 17  lookout            rare        A platform in the crown. The palm bends.
 18  spear_fishing      rare        A heroic lunge, a miss. The gull takes pity.

</pre>

The bottle gets a reply hours later, in a different bottle. The cat comes back another time. A kumara she plants grows quietly through the rest of the video, and nobody remarks on it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Sample List (F3)</b>: 0 samples, more than 150 sounds made of arithmetic</summary>
<br>

Every sound is synthesized from code in [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. There are more than 150 sound files so far.

- **Theme:** a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii, V, I, vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds: electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. Intro, groove, theme and breakdown, then round again.
- **Ocean:** also a seamless 60-second loop.
- **Levels:** the mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and every level can be set on the master and per routine.

Nobody has listened to it yet, so this list makes no claims about how it sounds.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Info Page (F5)</b>: what the screen up there is doing</summary>
<br>

- **The letters are the channels.** C is her, then the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore, the garden, the theme and the ocean. Each letter is that channel's pattern window, cut to shape, so a note only shows the part that fits. The green dots are empty cells.
- **One row per beat.** A tracker row lasts speed × 2.5 ÷ tempo seconds, so Speed 24 at tempo 80 is one row every 0.75 seconds: the rows step up in time with the theme, every fourth row (a bar line, where activities may start) is tinted, and the whole screen loops every 60 seconds, exactly where the theme does.
- **The minute shown** is staged and squeezed to fit, not captured from a run. It plays instrument 20, `leave_any_time`. The theme channel carries the theme's real chord roots, one per bar, the ocean loop retriggers on row 0, and the theme meter follows the real arrangement. On bar 3 she stands and stretches: one long note at volume 64. On bar 4 she walks off over the water: the volume column falls and her pan dot steps right, out of the window. On bar 8, note off. Channel 01 is then silent for 27 rows, which at one row a beat is the routine's twenty empty seconds, as near as rows allow. On row 55 she walks back in with an iced coffee, sits down and explains nothing.
- **Reduced motion** holds the frame at bar 11: her channel empty, the theme carrying on without her.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Song Message (Shift-F9)</b>: greetz and small print</summary>
<br>

Greetz to the cast: the cat (for the naps), the turtle (for the dozing), the shark (for keeping time), the hermit crab (now wearing a coconut), the hydrofoil bro (shaka received), the gull (for the pity fish) and whoever sells iced coffee out there (never explained).

Unhurried Tracker and Copra Software do not exist, and no rows were actually reserved. The screen is an original homage to the DOS text-mode trackers of the 1990s, such as Scream Tracker 3 and Impulse Tracker; no names, fonts or screens were copied from them. Castaway is an unofficial remake inspired by *Johnny Castaway* (1992), which belongs to its owners; its castaway does not appear here.

</details>
